practiceQuestions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of which of the following committees?
opts: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC was established by an executive resolution of the Central Government in February 1964 on the recommendations of the Committee on Prevention of Corruption, headed by K. Santhanam.

practiceQuestions.q: Initially, the Central Vigilance Commission was established as which type of body?
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, CVC was neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body; it was an executive agency. It was given statutory status in 2003 by an Act of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did the Parliament enact the Central Vigilance Commission Act granting it statutory status?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Parliament enacted the Central Vigilance Commission Act in 2003 (CVC Act, 2003) following the Supreme Court directions in the Vineet Narain case.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum number of Vigilance Commissioners that can be appointed to the CVC along with the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
opts: There is no maximum limit specified
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the CVC Act, the Commission consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson) and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners (members).

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following appoints the Central Vigilance Commissioner and other Vigilance Commissioners?
opts: President by warrant under his hand and seal
practiceQuestions.sol: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal on the recommendation of a high-power committee.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of office for the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners?
opts: 3 years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
4 years or 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
practiceQuestions.sol: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners hold office for a term of 4 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier (Note: Originally 5 years, amended by Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Act, 2021).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies is NOT represented on the committee that recommends names for appointment to the CVC?
opts: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The selection committee comprises the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Minister of Home Affairs (member), and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (member). The Chief Justice of India is not part of this committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Are the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government after ceasing to hold office?
opts: Yes, they can be re-appointed to the same office
Yes, they can take up any government post
No, they are not eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government
Yes, with the prior approval of the Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: To ensure independence and impartiality, the CVC and Vigilance Commissioners are not eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government after their tenure.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Central Vigilance Commission submit its annual report regarding its performance?
opts: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC presents an annual report on its performance to the President of India, who places it before each House of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the CVC Act 2003, the CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of which premier investigative agency in respect of corruption cases?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of the CBI in so far as it relates to the investigation of offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

practiceQuestions.q: How can the Central Vigilance Commissioner or any Vigilance Commissioner be removed from office before the expiry of their term?
opts: By the President on his own accord due to loss of confidence
By the President on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity, after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
By a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha alone
By the Prime Minister on the recommendation of the Union Cabinet
practiceQuestions.sol: The President can remove the CVC or any VC only on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity after the Supreme Court, on a reference made to it by the President, has, on inquiry, reported that they ought to be removed.

practiceQuestions.q: Which landmark Supreme Court judgment directed the government to grant statutory status to the CVC and place the CBI under its supervision?
opts: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997)
S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Vineet Narain case (1997), the Supreme Court gave detailed directions regarding executive control over CBI and directed that the CVC should be given statutory status to oversee CBI's functioning.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary role of the Central Vigilance Commission in the administrative hierarchy of India?
opts: Investigating criminal offenses independently like the police
Monitoring vigilance administration and advising central government organizations in planning and executing vigilance work
Auditing all government expenditures and financial accounts
Prosecuting corrupt officials directly in special corruption courts
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC is conceived as the apex body for exercising general superintendence over vigilance administration. It does not investigate crimes directly on its own (it outsources investigations to CBI or departmental chief vigilance officers) but guides and monitors policy.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the CVC Act, what category of central government employees falls under the direct jurisdiction of the CVC for inquiry/investigation guidance?
opts: Group C and D employees only
All-India Service officers and Group A officers of the Central Government
Only Cabinet Ministers and Members of Parliament
Private contractors dealing with the government
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC's jurisdiction covers members of All-India Services serving in the Union and Group 'A' officers of the Central Government, along with top executives of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks.

practiceQuestions.q: Which office assists the CVC in conducting inquiries into corruption complaints and functions as the investigative arm for cases referred to it?
practiceQuestions.sol: Every ministry or department has a Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) who assists the head of the department in vigilance matters. For serious cases, the CVC refers matters to the CBI or its own Commissioner for Departmental Inquiries (CDI).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) resolution, often associated with the CVC?
opts: It provides legal protection to whistleblowers who report corruption or misuse of office
It regulates political party funding transparency
It manages RTI applications across central ministries
It sets ethical codes for judicial appointments
practiceQuestions.sol: PIDPI (the Whistleblowers' Resolution) empowers the CVC to receive complaints against central government officials relating to corruption or misuse of office while keeping the identity of the whistleblower secret.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CVC ensure transparency and prevent corruption in major government procurements and tenders?
opts: By directly awarding all contracts itself
By appointing Independent External Monitors (IEMs) under the Integrity Pact
By fixing maximum price limits for all private market goods
By managing the GeM (Government e-Marketplace) portal directly
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC introduced the concept of the 'Integrity Pact' for major government purchases, monitored by Independent External Monitors (IEMs), to ensure transparency, equity, and elimination of corruption in tenders.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the nature of the recommendations given by the Central Vigilance Commission to government departments?
opts: Legally binding on all departments in every circumstance
Advisory in nature, though departments must record reasons if they depart from them
Binding only if approved by the Supreme Court
Purely recommendatory with no administrative consequences for non-compliance
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC's functions are primarily advisory. However, if a government department differs from the CVC's advice in disciplinary matters, it has to explain the reasons for such departure, and cases of non-acceptance are reported in the CVC's annual report.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Act passed in 2021?
opts: To extend the tenure of the Director of CBI and Director of Enforcement up to a maximum of 5 years
To merge the CVC with the Lokpal
To remove the requirement of parliamentary approval for CVC rules
To allow the Chief Justice of India to head the CVC selection committee
practiceQuestions.sol: The 2021 amendment to the CVC Act (and Delhi Special Police Establishment Act) enabled the extension of the tenure of the CBI Director and ED Director from two years to up to five years in public interest, through annual extensions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a limitation or critique commonly leveled against the Central Vigilance Commission?
opts: It has independent prosecuting powers like the CBI
It is often described as a 'toothless tiger' because it lacks its own independent investigative machinery and relies heavily on CBI or departmental CVOs
It controls the state police forces across all states in India
It audits the Comptroller and Auditor General's accounts
practiceQuestions.sol: Critics often call the CVC a 'toothless tiger' because it has no independent investigating staff of its own and has to depend on the CBI or departmental vigilance machinery for probes.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):
1. It was originally established in 1964 by an executive resolution of the Central Government.
2. It acquired statutory status with the enactment of the CVC Act, 2003.
3. It is a multi-member body consisting of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than five Vigilance Commissioners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the CVC consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and *not more than two* Vigilance Commissioners (not five).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment and composition of the CVC selection committee:
1. The Prime Minister is the chairperson of the committee.
2. The Minister of Law and Justice is a mandatory member of the committee.
3. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member of the committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (PM is Chairperson). Statement 3 is correct (Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha is a member). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Minister of Home Affairs (not Law and Justice) is the second member of this three-member committee.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Central Vigilance Commissioner:
1. The President can remove the CVC on the ground of proved misbehavior without any prior judicial inquiry.
2. The Supreme Court must hold an inquiry and report that the CVC ought to be removed before the President can effect such removal.
3. The CVC can be removed by a simple majority vote in both Houses of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because a Supreme Court inquiry is mandatory. Statement 3 is incorrect because removal does not happen via parliamentary resolution; it follows the Supreme Court inquiry report and Presidential order.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions and powers of the CVC:
1. It can conduct inquiries into offenses committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by public servants under its jurisdiction.
2. It has the power to call for reports, returns, and statements from central government ministries or departments to monitor vigilance work.
3. It directly controls and directs the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) for all money laundering investigations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because while CVC exercises superintendence over CBI regarding Prevention of Corruption Act cases, its superintendence over ED is limited to certain specific aspects under the CVC Act and does not amount to direct day-to-day control of all money laundering investigations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the CVC and the CBI:
1. The CVC exercises superintendence over the CBI in investigation of corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
2. The CVC recommends panels of names for the appointment of CBI Director under the DSPE Act.
3. The CBI Director is appointed by the Central Government directly without any consultation with the CVC committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the CBI Director is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge), and the CVC plays a key role in recommending the panel under the DSPE Act.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure and re-appointment of the CVC and Vigilance Commissioners:
1. They hold office for a term of 4 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. Upon ceasing to hold office, they are eligible for appointment to any ministerial or diplomatic post under the Central Government.
3. They are not eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government after retirement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because they are barred from any further employment under the Central or State Government after ceasing to hold office.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding whistleblower protection in India in relation to the CVC:
1. The Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) resolution empowers the CVC to act as the designated agency to receive complaints on corruption.
2. The CVC is legally mandated to reveal the identity of the whistleblower to the accused officer during departmental inquiries to ensure fair trial.
3. The Whistleblowers Protection Act provides statutory backing to whistleblower complaints, though its full implementation framework involves designated authorities like the CVC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the CVC is strictly mandated to *protect* the identity of the whistleblower and does not reveal it to anyone, ensuring confidentiality.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural evolution and independence of the CVC:
1. The Supreme Court in the Vineet Narain case (1997) emphasized the need for institutionalizing the CVC to insulate it from political interference.
2. Following the 2003 CVC Act, the Commission became completely financially autonomous with its budget charged directly upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. The salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service of the Central Vigilance Commissioner are akin to those of the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The CVC's salary and service conditions are equated with the UPSC Chairman (for CVC) and UPSC Members (for VCs). Statement 2 is incorrect because its expenses are met from parliamentary appropriations (voted) rather than being charged directly on the Consolidated Fund of India like CAG or UPSC.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction and scope of the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. The CVC has jurisdiction over all employees of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and public sector banks.
2. The CVC has direct original investigative powers over state government officials accused of corruption within state territories.
3. The CVC advises the central government departments on appropriate disciplinary action against erring officers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the CVC has jurisdiction only over central government employees and specified categories of central public sector bodies; it does not have jurisdiction over state government officials acting within state domains (who fall under State Vigilance Commissions and Lokayuktas).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Integrity Pact' promoted by the CVC:
1. It is an agreement between the prospective vendors/contractors and the government buyer committing both sides to refrain from bribery and corrupt practices.
2. Independent External Monitors (IEMs) are appointed to oversee the implementation and compliance of Integrity Pacts in major public procurement contracts.
3. The Integrity Pact is legally binding under international law and enforced directly by the International Court of Justice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Integrity Pact is a tool implemented within domestic public procurement frameworks under the guidance of CVC and Transparency International, not enforced by the International Court of Justice.
